acceptanceCriteria: Phase M is a sealed configuration-only mitigation with TWO literal diff universes and no self-referential manifest: the DEPLOYABLE universe is the diff from the M base commit to the M source commit and contains exactly rows M1 add samples/meeting-room/wrangler.g32-final-receiver.jsonc#/workers_dev value false; M2 add samples/meeting-room/wrangler.g32-final-receiver.jsonc#/preview_urls value false; M3 new file scripts/deploy/g38-m-witness.mjs; M4 new file scripts/deploy/g38-m-witness.d.mts; M5 add package.json#/scripts/g38:m:witness value node scripts/deploy/g38-m-witness.mjs; M7 new file contracts/g38-m-change-manifest.json. The EVIDENCE-ONLY universe is the diff from the M source commit to the M evidence completion commit and contains exactly row M6 new file docs/SDT-G38-m-evidence.json — the deployable preflight must NOT require M6 (evidence cannot exist before the deploy) and the postflight must FAIL when M6 is absent. The manifest file lists rows M1-M7 with rowId, path, JSON pointer or whole-file marker, and change kind for all rows, expected values for M1, M2 and M5, and for its own row M7 NO embedded full-bytes expected value: the manifest's identity is anchored EXTERNALLY by the packet-side fixed (rowId, path, changeKind) set plus a canonical-core digest whose formula is EXACTLY sha256(UTF8(sekiban-dcb-ts/g38-m-change-manifest/v1) || 0x00 || RFC8785(project(manifest))), where project is the REMOVAL (deletion, not null-replacement) of the single top-level JSON pointer /selfDigest, the output form is the string sha256: followed by lowercase hexadecimal, and the M evidence binds that digest together with the M source commit; an absent, renamed or additional self-digest field is rejected. Count and set equality is asserted PER UNIVERSE; an unused row, an extra path, a renamed file, an extra package.json script key, a value differing from the expected value, a preflight that demands M6 before deploy, a postflight that passes without M6, an unverified M7 self identity, a digest computed with a substituted algorithm, a digest computed without the domain separator, a projection that null-replaces instead of deleting /selfDigest, an uppercase or differently-encoded digest string, and an alternate, missing or extra self-digest field each fail alone, and the deployable diff against runtime code, Durable Object bindings, Durable Object migrations, queue configuration and database configuration is byte zero. M is sealed with its own base commit, source commit, config digest and deploy identity. The exposure witness covers BOTH preview URL families: pre-M captures the receiver's workers.dev URL, the set of active VERSIONED preview URLs and the set of ALIASED preview URLs from the remote version and alias registry; post-M re-checks every captured member and separately reads the live workers_dev and preview settings back from the remote registry; an empty captured set is acceptable ONLY together with a passing remote settings read-back. The M public-surface invariant is re-checked at C, at R, at PR head, and thereafter on the scheduled cadence of AC3's operational contract for as long as the old Worker is retained; a witness that checks one arbitrary hostname, a witness whose captured set post-dates the change, and a C-phase diff that flips workers_dev or preview_urls back each fail alone. The evidence states explicitly that phase M does NOT close the fence split of AC4.

Primary-only component guard with a CLOSED profile universe recorded as an artifact: the command route, the bootstrap operator route, the repair operator route and the conformance route each check the deployment component fail-closed at entry, so a request arriving where G32_COMPONENT is receiver, missing, or unknown receives an exact typed reject with zero downstream calls into the domain handler, the runtime, any Durable Object, D1 or the queue, while the named entrypoint MeetingRoomDownstreamDoorbell.deliver() is proven by a separate fixture to remain permitted. The profile universe is the new artifact contracts/g38-profile-table.json (schemaVersion 1) whose rows carry EXACTLY the literal fields (configPath, workerName, main, component, deploymentPermission, reachableLanes) — deploymentPermission drawn from the closed enum permitted / forbidden-after-g30-closeout / forbidden, with NO other state vocabulary anywhere in the three documents (the words supported and retired are prose only if they appear at all; the machine fields are these literals) — and liveness carried NOWHERE in the profile table: generation liveness is owned by the SEALED phase-indexed generation contract of AC7 and selected by the evidence ledger of AC6, because remote witnesses occur only after candidate C is sealed and no contract file may change after C — because a configuration row's cardinality cannot express generations: the G30 runbook deploys the primary THREE times (A off, B on, A-prime off), so the B/on generation is already superseded before this packet while the A-prime/off generation stays live until AC3 step (b), and the receiver-off generation stays live until step (e); closing issue SDT-G30 ends only the permission to redeploy, never a generation's liveness, and whose content covers EVERY configuration in the repository whose main is src/worker.cloudflare-only.ts at the dependency head: wrangler.g32-final-primary.jsonc (deploymentPermission permitted, primary), the new receiver configuration of AC3 (deploymentPermission permitted, receiver), wrangler.g30-primary-off.jsonc and wrangler.g30-primary-on.jsonc (deploymentPermission forbidden-after-g30-closeout, primary, deployed by scripts/deploy/g30-b0-deploy.sh and reachable from scripts/g30-config-check.mjs and the test:g30 lane; the A-prime/off generation is recorded live until SUPERSEDED at AC3 step (b) and the B/on generation is recorded superseded BEFORE this packet, both witnessed by remote deployment versions, never by issue status), wrangler.g30-receiver-off.jsonc (deploymentPermission forbidden-after-g30-closeout, receiver, same reachability; its generation stays live until DELETED at AC3 step (e)), and the six older configurations (wrangler.cloudflare-only.jsonc, wrangler.cloudflare-only-doorbell.jsonc, wrangler.direct-doorbell.jsonc, wrangler.doorbell.jsonc, wrangler.meeting-room-doorbell.jsonc, wrangler.meeting-room-doorbell-production.jsonc) with deploymentPermission forbidden — deployment is forbidden from this packet's cutoff onward, while their historical deployments (G20, G26, G29, G31 deploy scripts) remain recorded facts, not contradictions. The gate asserts row count and set equality between the artifact and the configurations discovered in the tree, every row whose deploymentPermission is not permitted is asserted undeployable (no deploy script outside the G30 runbook names it and CI has no deploy lane for it), and every lane that boots the shared module sets G32_COMPONENT explicitly and appears in reachableLanes; the G15 local E2E boots wrangler.jsonc whose main is src/worker.ts and is outside the guard surface (stated, not assumed). Removing the guard from EACH of the four entries fails alone, as do a guard that treats missing as primary, a guard that admits an unknown value, a guard that rejects the named delivery entrypoint, deletion of any one of the three G30 rows, promotion of any row whose deploymentPermission is not permitted to a deploy input, a deploy of a configuration whose deploymentPermission is forbidden, a mutation that flips the G30 rows to absence expectations on issue close alone, a mutation that marks two primary generations live simultaneously, a mutation that marks the B/on generation live, a mutation that reintroduces a liveness field into the profile table, a mutation that uses a state word outside the declared enum as a machine value, a mutation that retires the primary generation before step (b), and a mutation that retires the receiver generation before step (e), and an enumerated lane left without an explicit component. Module separation (AC3) and this guard are independent defences; neither substitutes for the other.

Receiver-only entry module deployed as a NEW Worker with a NORMATIVE cutover order and a closure-consistent retirement contract: the receiver-only module (exporting exactly the named entrypoint MeetingRoomDownstreamDoorbell and nothing else, with no default fetch export) is deployed under the new Worker name sekiban-dcb-meeting-room-doorbell-g38, whose configuration declares NO durable_objects bindings other than the external BOOTSTRAP of AC4, NO migrations key, and workers_dev false with preview URLs disabled FROM ITS FIRST DEPLOYMENT. The cutover follows this order and each step is witnessed: (a) deploy the new receiver FIRST and read back from the remote registry its named entrypoint, its never-public settings and its external BOOTSTRAP binding; (b) deploy the primary with its service binding retargeted to the new Worker; (c) read the primary's active deployment from the remote deployments API and assert it is EXACTLY the one-element set {(newVersionId, 100)} whose version id equals the deploy identity recorded at step (b) — this proves all NEW routing targets the new version, while invocations already started are the subject of step (d); (d) prove the old receiver INERT rather than proving a timed quiescence, because the platform sets no wall-time bound on a request whose caller stays connected (the 30-second rule governs only waitUntil after response), so no finite wait can prove that an already-started invocation has ended: the old Worker is first TOMBSTONED (see d6) and live-inert is then a MACHINE-READABLE CONJUNCTION over the ENUMERATED account-wide trigger universe, every class compared against provider state — (d1) zero incoming service bindings (the account-wide binding graph scan showing the old primary version was the only referencer, so after step (c) no new binding invocation can begin); (d2) zero public exposure: workers.dev disabled, preview URLs disabled, zero routes and zero custom domains (the phase-M witness re-read extended to routes and domains); (d3) zero queue consumer registrations; (d4) zero cron triggers; (d5) zero tail or other event bindings; (d6) alarms are neutralized STRUCTURALLY, not enumerated, because getAlarm is a storage operation executable only inside each object and the account API exposes no per-object alarm state: after step (c) a TOMBSTONE VERSION is deployed to the old Worker — it retains all four Durable Object classes so the namespaces are preserved, exports NO default fetch, answers its named entrypoint with a typed frozen error (the G32 bridge frozen pattern), and implements every alarm handler as delete-the-alarm-and-return with NO external call, NO durable business mutation OTHER THAN the alarm deletion itself, and NO reschedule, so any pending or retried alarm self-neutralizes on first firing; bounded residual activity is ILLEGAL — there is no acceptance branch — and the closure oracle uses the SAME literal deployment witness as the primary: the old Worker's deployments API result must be EXACTLY the one-element set {(tombstoneVersionId, 100)} with tombstoneVersionId equal to the upload identity sealed in C evidence — a deployment below 100 percent MAY leave some retained objects, including pending-alarm objects, assigned to the OLD version, and only the exact singleton at 100 percent EXCLUDES that possibility — and the witness binds the tombstone version's four exported class identities and namespace ids; it fails closed when sole-active assignment cannot be established; an UNKNOWN trigger class in the provider inventory fails closed, and one mutation or fixture per trigger class plus these alarm fixtures each fail alone: a pending Tag alarm firing into the tombstone (no external calls, alarm deleted), a pending Journal alarm likewise, an at-least-once retry delivery, a tombstone handler that attempts a reschedule, a tombstone handler that touches D1 or a Queue or a service binding, and a closure claimed while the old Worker still runs the pre-tombstone version; this deployment family has ALREADY drifted through exactly these classes (a live per-minute cron and an undeclared queue consumer were found on 2026-08-23), so checked-in bindings are not an acceptable authority; a telemetry query over the old receiver MAY be recorded as ADVISORY evidence with request and response stored verbatim and is explicitly NON-AUTHORITATIVE — treating it as closure authority is itself a failing mutation; (e) the old Worker sekiban-dcb-meeting-room-doorbell is RETAINED INERT at closure — never-public, zero referencers, its four namespaces intact — and this packet's CLOSURE PHASE is post-b with the inert old receiver present in the expected graph; the eventual deletion is a POST-CLOSURE operator action, NOT a closure gate and NOT scheduled by any timer: when the operator performs it, it follows the sealed deletion contract — the Worker delete operation with its force parameter value RECORDED (force true acknowledges destruction of the four receiver-local Durable Object namespaces, destruction already approved by this packet), a preflight that re-runs the reference scan and asserts it empty, and evidence comprising the delete response, absence from the remote Worker registry AND absence of the four namespaces from the account's Durable Object namespace listing (an HTTP 404 alone is NOT acceptable because the hostname returns 404 from phase M onward) — and the witness is appended to the cutover ledger as step e, moving the expected graph to post-e. ROLLBACK is classified BY PHASE, every transition bound to BOTH the ledger prefix AND the old Worker's current active deployment identity, because the tombstone deployment is a linearization point inside the pre-closure interval: (r0) PRE-TOMBSTONE candidate abort — before the tombstone is the sole active version, retargeting the primary's binding back to the still-functional old Worker aborts candidate C and returns to the pre-closure system; (r1) POST-TOMBSTONE, PRE-CLOSURE abort — once the tombstone is sole-active, the old Worker is frozen and retargeting to it produces failures, not the pre-closure system, so the abort path MUST stay on a receiver-only, never-public Worker with the external primary BOOTSTRAP authority, and restoring the old shared module to the old Worker is a CLOSURE-PREVENTING emergency degradation, never an abort; (r2) AFTER post-b closure, retargeting to the old Worker is an EMERGENCY DEGRADATION that RETRACTS this unit's closure even though the Worker is not deleted — the tombstone makes it structurally non-functional as a receiver, so such a retarget also cannot silently restore the old split behaviour; (r3) a CLOSURE-PRESERVING rollback at any phase after closure must use a receiver-only, never-public Worker with the external primary BOOTSTRAP authority (redeploying the receiver-only module under a receiver identity); (r4) after step e the same r3 rule applies. A post-b retarget labelled closure-preserving, a ledger selector left at post-b after such a retarget, rollback evidence that omits the closure retraction, a post-tombstone retarget to the frozen Worker labelled a pre-closure abort, a silent restoration of the old shared module, and a missing barrier fixture at tombstone-deploy-success with evidence-append-failure each fail alone, and reverting to the OLD pre-tombstone configuration (local namespaces, shared module) is always an emergency degradation, never a rollback that keeps AC2 and AC4 satisfied. A primary-first deployment, a deletion executed as part of closure or on a timer, a deletion without the re-run reference preflight, a missing or partial check of ANY live-inert trigger class, an unknown trigger class treated as acceptable, a tombstone deployment split below 100 percent, a 100 percent assignment carrying the wrong version id, a tombstone missing one of the four classes, a namespace-id drift, closure evidence captured before the tombstone became the sole active version, an advisory telemetry record treated as closure authority, a deployment version mismatch at step (c), a deletion with a remaining external reference, a deletion evidenced by 404 alone, a new-Worker configuration that declares a migrations key or a local Durable Object class, an old-Worker closure state OTHER THAN live-inert (an active old Worker and a deleted-at-closure old Worker both fail), and a rollback record that claims closure is preserved after reverting to the old configuration each fail alone. The retained Worker and its four namespaces are INTENTIONAL RESOURCES governed by a SEALED OPERATIONAL MANIFEST contracts/g38-retention-ops.json that states literals, not intentions: the owner identity in the exact format operator:<email>; the schedule as the literal cron expression 0 3 * * 1 (weekly) implemented by a candidate-C GitHub workflow that re-runs the live-inert conjunction and the M public-surface invariant; a maximum evidence age of 8 days measured from the checkedAt timestamp of the newest entry in docs/SDT-G38-evidence-retention.jsonl; the exact account id, Worker name and namespace ids; the storage metric surface sealed as an EXACT GraphQL query contract: the durableObjectsStorageGroups dataset with the max { storedBytes } aggregation, the account selector, the namespace dimension and filter field taken from PINNED introspection output, per-namespace row identity with count and set equality across ALL FOUR namespace ids (an account-level aggregate is not acceptable — it can hide one namespace's growth or fail on an unrelated namespace's), stated pagination and limit behaviour, a 7-day query window and byte units; the closure baseline storedBytes per namespace recorded at closure with a permitted delta of ZERO growth, where the explanation allowlist is FINITE and PROSPECTIVE — each entry names a namespace id, a maximum permitted delta, a reason and an expiry, and an unused, unknown or expired entry fails, so growth can never be explained after the fact; the evidence path docs/SDT-G38-evidence-retention.jsonl and its row schema, whose appends follow the SAME git-ref fast-forward CAS as the cutover ledger with prefix revalidation on conflict, a unique runId per scheduled run (a duplicate runId fails), and mutations proving that a truncation, an overwrite of an existing line, a duplicate run identity, and a lost concurrent append each fail independently; and the failure outcome (the scheduled lane turns red and stays red until resolved). Because a scheduled workflow cannot detect its own non-execution (a disabled schedule, a removed cron or an expired credential produces NO run to evaluate), the manifest names an INDEPENDENT WATCHDOG AUTHORITY that is an EXPLICIT HOST-SIDE PREREQUISITE, not a behaviour ascribed to the generic supervision loop and not deliverable by target candidate C: the sealed host script intents/sekiban-dcb-ts/contracts/g38_retention_watchdog.py, whose contract fixes the target repository and workflow identity (J-Tech-Japan/sekiban-dcb-ts, g38-retention.yml), the evidence path and row schema it reads, the credential contract (an authenticated gh CLI; a missing credential is a typed failure BEFORE any query), a cadence of at most 4 days, the escalation transport (an operator-facing escalation through the host notify surface), and an INSTALLATION AND LIVENESS WITNESS — the closure evidence must include the host scheduler registration listing and the watchdog's first successful run output; the watchdog's absence, a disabled schedule, a wrong repository or workflow, a stale credential, and an inability to read the evidence each fail INDEPENDENTLY of the workflow's own lane; the watchdog's evidence validation is itself FAIL-CLOSED: an exact row schema (runId, checkedAt, workflowRunId, headSha, conclusion, cIdentity, namespaceSamples — a missing key and an unknown key each fail), runId uniqueness over the WHOLE prefix, rejection of a checkedAt more than a sealed 300-second skew in the future (a fabricated far-future timestamp can never hold the watchdog green), and the newest row BOUND to the newest trusted successful workflow run by run id, head SHA and conclusion and to the sealed C identity; a missing gh executable, a malformed API or base64 response and an unauthorized response after auth succeed as typed machine-readable findings, never tracebacks; the watchdog binds evidence to a SEALED EXPECTED-IDENTITY SOURCE (contracts/g38-watchdog-expected.json): while it holds the UNSEALED placeholder the watchdog fails typed as expected-unsealed (closure seals the real C identity and the four namespace ids into it), the newest row's cIdentity must equal the sealed expectation, and namespaceSamples is an exact schema (namespaceId, storedBytes) whose id multiset equals the four sealed namespace ids — an empty, missing, extra or duplicate sample each fails; and a NINETEEN-CASE committed fixture battery with a manifest of exact case names, expected exit codes and expected findings (healthy baseline, future timestamp, missing key, unknown key, duplicate runId, mismatched run binding, malformed ledger line, stale credential, wrong C identity, expected-unsealed, empty samples, extra sample, duplicate sample, unauthorized workflow API, unauthorized runs API, malformed workflow JSON, malformed runs JSON, malformed base64 content, missing gh tooling) runs under --self-test with fixture-injected transport and a fixture-scoped clock, NEVER querying production, and asserts each negative case emits exactly its expected findings while the baseline alone returns success; a missing workflow invocation, a disabled workflow, a missing credential before the query, and stale evidence with no scheduled run each fail INDEPENDENTLY of the workflow's own lane. The scheduled workflow file itself is a candidate-C artifact, and a schedule removal, a cadence enlargement, a stale checkedAt, an owner removal or rename, a namespace omission, a metric field substitution, an account-aggregate substituted for per-namespace rows, a missing sample, a namespace-count mismatch, a baseline reset, a positive storage delta without a valid prospective allowlist entry, and a watchdog removal each fail alone.

Bootstrap route admission has a single authority across components: the NEW receiver's BOOTSTRAP binding is an EXTERNAL binding whose script_name names the primary's deployed Worker (sekiban-dcb-meeting-room-cloudflare-only), and the new receiver declares no ALLOCATOR, JOURNAL or TAG binding; the defect being closed is that an INDEPENDENT authority decides admission — which can produce both a false admit while the primary is importing and a false reject of a delivery the primary would accept — not the incidental EMPTY state observed on 2026-08-23, which static code cannot prove permanent. The oracle drives the primary's BootstrapCoordinatorDurableObject through every non-admit state (PLANNED, IMPORTING, VERIFYING, FAILED) and asserts a receiver fast delivery receives the SAME typed outcome as a primary-side fast delivery in that state, and through EMPTY and READY and asserts both admit in both components; a mutation that removes script_name, a mutation that points script_name at a different Worker, a mutation that deletes the BOOTSTRAP binding entirely, and a mutation that re-adds a local ALLOCATOR, JOURNAL or TAG binding each fail alone with its own message. The env.BOOTSTRAP undefined early return in admitBootstrapRoute is a TYPED FAILURE for any component that declares a doorbell delivery role, so removing the binding can never be a silent success — the exact state the retired G26 receiver was in.

Conformance passthrough is allowlisted, proven by TWO oracles neither of which is vacuous: (a) on the RECEIVER, the conformance route and the default fetch export are structurally absent, proven by export-surface assertion and by route resolution failing before any handler branch is reached — this oracle asserts absence, not a zero port count, because after AC3 a port count of zero is trivially true; (b) on the PRIMARY, a request carrying a VALID conformance bearer with an unknown suffix and with each runtime control suffix (internal/downstream/drain, journals/{attemptId}, tags/{serviceId}/{tag}, bootstrap/{serviceId}, operator/...) reaches the allowlist reject branch and produces an exact typed outcome with a ZERO-CALL assertion on runtimeFetch and on every raw runtime, Durable Object, D1 and queue port. A mutation that widens the allowlist to a prefix match, a mutation that forwards an unknown suffix, and a mutation that allowlists a runtime control route each fail alone on the primary oracle, and a mutation that restores a conformance export on the receiver fails alone on the receiver oracle.

Remote topology is reconciled against ONE concrete declared authority with byte-fixed digests and separated input semantics: the expected topology artifact contracts/deployment-topology-expected.json (schemaVersion 1) is generated by scripts/g38-topology-expected.mjs, whose inputs are the AC2 profile table with its state semantics ENFORCED — the artifact is sealed in candidate C and contains FOUR PHASE-INDEXED expected graphs keyed pre-cutover, post-a, post-b and post-e — each a full (producer set, consumer set, dead-letter target, Worker-name set) with the G30 A-prime/off and receiver-off generations present in pre-cutover, the new receiver appearing at post-a, the primary retargeted at post-b — which is this packet's CLOSURE PHASE and carries the old receiver as live-inert — and the old receiver absent only at post-e, which is reached by the post-closure deletion — and the remote gate SELECTS the applicable graph through the TOTAL literal mapping none maps to pre-cutover, a maps to post-a, and b, c and d ALL map to post-b (steps c and d witness properties of the post-b topology, not new topologies), and e maps to post-e — so every ledger state has exactly one graph — by reading the append-only evidence ledger docs/SDT-G38-evidence-cutover.jsonl, whose name matches the post-C allowlist and which is an EXACT PREFIX STATE MACHINE: JSON Lines, one witnessed step per line, unique step ids drawn from a b c d e, strictly monotone in that order with no skipped, repeated or conflicting step, strictly increasing timestamps, each payload bound to the C identity and the relevant deployment and version ids, and appended only through an ATOMIC compare-and-swap whose linearization point is the git branch ref update: an append is a commit that adds exactly one ledger line, its durability is the accepted (fast-forward) push of that commit, a concurrent writer's push is rejected as non-fast-forward and that loser MUST reload the ledger and revalidate the entire prefix before retrying (a line count is not a compare authority because equal-length content can conflict), and no phase may be selected from a ledger line whose commit has not been accepted; contract files NEVER change after C and a graph is asserted only for the phase selected by the durable ledger; a BARRIER RACE oracle has two writers propose different payloads for the same step and asserts exactly one becomes durable while the loser cannot select a phase and can never contribute a live Worker or queue edge. The artifact digest is SHA-256 over the byte sequence UTF8(sekiban-dcb-ts/deployment-topology-expected/v1) || 0x00 || RFC8785(JSON) in exactly that order. The G38 remote gate consumes the artifact and its digest, fetches the live registry, and compares; it enforces liveAccountWorkers EQUALS sampleDeclaredWorkers DISJOINT-UNION exclusions, where each exclusion carries identity, reason and expiry; an expired, unknown or unused exclusion, an extra or missing remote consumer, an extra remote producer, a wrong dead-letter target, an undeclared deployed Worker, and — for the retained live-inert Worker — any trigger class of the AC3 conjunction (route, custom domain, queue consumer, cron, tail or event binding, workers.dev or preview exposure) found attached in provider state, and an old Worker whose active deployment is not exactly {(tombstoneVersionId, 100)} each fail alone, as do a mutation that checks producers only, a mutation that checks only the queues the current profile names, a contract or profile or generation-contract write after C, a ledger step c or d left unmapped by the selector, a skipped predecessor step, a duplicate or conflicting step, a timestamp reversal, a payload bound to the wrong C, a selector consulted before the durable append completes, a future phase's graph selected before its witness exists, a closure graph that still references the deleted receiver, and a live G30 generation dropped from the pre-cutover graph on issue close alone, and a PREIMAGE with the domain and JSON order reversed. When G34 Unit A lands, absorption is an EXECUTABLE single-authority procedure: the old generator is run from its sealed parent commit, the new generator's output is byte-compared against it, the migration commit's tree contains ONLY the new producer, and the consumer's pin and digest switch in that same commit; an artifact rename, both producers surviving the migration commit, and a dual-run reported as passed without actually executing the old generator each fail alone.

Deploy inventory is validated against a machine-defined universe whose SOURCE-ROOT MANIFEST is itself a sealed artifact: contracts/g38-inventory-source-roots.json (schemaVersion 1) enumerates, with one rowId per root: (1) the wrangler glob root samples/meeting-room/wrangler*.jsonc evaluated across the FULL git history from the repository root commit to the dependency head with rename following, (2) the deploy-literal scanner over scripts/deploy with its worker-name pattern stated literally, (3) the dated remote registry snapshot with its capture date, account identity and content digest, and (4) an independent CURATED SEED LIST naming the worker generations already known to this packet (the G32-final pair, the g38 successor, the G29/G31/G32-bridge generations under the old receiver name, the G26 pair, sekiban-dcb-g20-negative-oracle) so that shrinking the derived universe and the inventory together still fails against the seed. The gate requires a full-history (non-shallow) checkout and asserts THREE equalities: the source-root manifest's row set against the roots the generator actually consumed, the derived universe against the union of root outputs plus the curated seed, and the derived universe against the rows of the SEALED generation contract contracts/g38-deploy-inventory.json — part of candidate C, immutable after C, keyed by (workerName, generation), each row recording the generation's source, its declaring configuration path or null, its remote queue roles, and its EXPECTED STATE PER PHASE (pre-cutover / post-a / post-b / post-e) drawn from live / live-inert / superseded-by SUCCESSOR-ROW-ID / deleted / never-deployed, the old receiver being live-inert at post-b (the closure phase) under its tombstone version with namespaces preserved, and deleted only at post-e — while the OBSERVED transitions and their post-conditions are recorded separately in the append-only, allowlist-compatible evidence ledger docs/SDT-G38-evidence-inventory.jsonl, and the gate joins ledger entries to contract rows so that every expected transition has its witness and no witness lacks an expected transition. The already-completed retirements are contract rows whose witnesses are recorded in the ledger, and the old receiver's deletion is an expected post-e transition that is POST-CLOSURE: its witness lands in the ledger whenever the operator performs it, and closure is assessed at post-b. A row omission, a source-root omission, a snapshot swapped for a different date or account, a shallow clone, a seed entry missing from the derived universe, an unknown live Worker, a witnessed transition without its expected contract row, an expected transition asserted without its witness, and a superseded row pointing at a nonexistent successor each fail alone.

Primary and delivery non-regression proven WITHOUT a production write: the primary's configuration is compared to its pre-change state by EXACT FILE DIGEST with a field-level allowlist whose only permitted change in phase C is the service binding target renaming sekiban-dcb-meeting-room-doorbell to sekiban-dcb-meeting-room-doorbell-g38; the V1 wire is unchanged and G13 golden output has a byte-zero diff; direct doorbell delivery keeps running on the receiver in separate mode with the same delivery class, allowed views, max invocation bound and degradation setting. The end-to-end write path is proven on an ISOLATED non-production serviceId and provider, never by issuing a new command against production; production evidence is restricted to read-only GETs, configuration and remote topology reads, service-binding edge verification, and read-only telemetry of traffic that already exists. A mutation that changes the primary's queue bindings, a mutation that flips DIRECT_DOORBELL_RECEIVER_MODE, a mutation that alters the delivery class, a mutation that widens the primary field allowlist, and a mutation that reintroduces a production write into any closure oracle each fail alone.

Phase ordering is enforced and phase C follows the candidate protocol with the M invariant carried forward: the M evidence completion commit is a PRECONDITION of sealing C; C/R evidence carries the identities of M, C and R together; the AC3 cutover order (new receiver first, primary retarget, 100 percent single-version confirmation, inertness witnesses) is part of the C evidence with its steps in order, and step e — the deletion — is explicitly POST-CLOSURE, absent from the closure evidence and appended to the ledger only when performed; the M public-surface invariant is re-witnessed against BOTH receiver identities after C — the retained-inert old Worker (until its eventual post-closure deletion) and the new Worker from its first deployment — so the invariant survives the identity change and the retention; phase C is the structural change under the non-self-referential candidate protocol (final C sealed ONCE after all fixes carries all runtime, config, CI, docs, tools and manifests as deployment and digest authority; evidence records sourceCommit equal to C plus tree digests; the post-C allowlist is limited to docs/SDT-G38-*evidence*.{json,jsonl,md} plus the single ci.yml retained-list append by bookkeeping commit R — the append-only ledgers are .jsonl and their steady-state appends are legal post-C diffs by this exact rule; any other post-C diff requires a new C with full re-verification; retention is checked at R and at PR head).
